title: P1C3 - SEBI, Company Law & CSR

contentText: Syllabus (GS3):  SEBI, financial-stability bodies, company types & corporate governance, CSR, takeovers. 1. SEBI SEBI:  formed 1988 (executive order) -> statutory body 1992; powers widened 1999 & 2014 (can search, seize, attach property, arrest). HQ Mumbai. Board:  Chairman + 1 RBI officer + 2 Union Govt officers + members appointed by Govt. Chairman up to 5 yr / 65 age (reappointment possible). Regulates:  Process (issuing bonds/shares/IPO/ETF/REIT/InvIT under Securities Contracts Regulation Act 1956), Places (depositories, exchanges), Persons (investors, brokers, fund managers), and any Collective Investment Scheme >= Rs.100 cr (post-Sahara/chit-fund). Appeals:  Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) -> Supreme Court (SAT also hears IRDAI & PFRDA appeals). Investor tools:  SCORES complaint portal (v2.0, justice in 21 days), SMARTs trainer program, Saarthi awareness app. Chiefs:  10th Madhabi Puri Buch (2022-25); 11th Tuhin Kanta Pandey (IAS, 2025, 3-yr). Pratyush Sinha Committee (2025):  to prevent SEBI conflict-of-interest (after Hindenburg's Adani allegation vs Madhabi Buch). Q - Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025? Before After the Bill 3 laws: SCRA 1956, SEBI Act 1992, Depositories Act 1996 Merged into one Securities Markets Code SEBI board = 9 (5 'other members') 'Other members' 5 -> 11; total board = 15 Weak conflict-of-interest rules Members must disclose family business interests & recuse; new SEBI-Ombudsman Even minor offences -> jail Minor offences decriminalized (fine only) 2. Investor Protection & Capital-Market Depth Investor Charter (Budget-2021, notified 2021):  commitments to investors across products/events (IPO, mutual funds, REITs, InvITs etc.). Why protect investors:  scams erode savings (social ills), push money into gold/real estate (raises imports, black money); more retail participation = 'deepening the capital market' -> factory expansion, jobs, growth (and less pressure on bank loans). Public shareholding:  min 25% public holding in listed Govt companies (Budget-2019); SEBI aimed 35% for private. ES25 - capital market deepened:  investors 4.9 cr (2020) -> 13.2 cr; MF accounts 2.9 -> 5.6 cr; SIP Rs.0.10 -> Rs.0.23 lakh cr/month; IPOs 196 -> 250+; India = 30% of global IPOs (2024). But ES25 also flags the  bond market as under-developed  (India corp-bond ~18% of GDP vs China 36%, Korea 80%; insurers/pension funds can't buy below-AA bonds; 60% of bonds issued by banks/NBFCs; weak secondary liquidity). Bond Central Portal (2025):  SEBI's one-stop database of all corporate bonds (via OBPP Association). SWAGAT-FI window (2025):  Single Window Automatic & Generalised Access for Trusted foreign investors - low-risk FPI registration valid 10 yr (was 3-5). FPI = <=10% stake; FDI = >10%. 3. Financial-Stability Bodies Q - FSDC (2010)? Financial Stability & Development Council:  supervises the economy & large financial conglomerates, coordinates regulators, financial literacy/inclusion. Chair = Finance Minister; members = MoS Finance, heads of RBI/SEBI/IRDAI/PFRDA/IFSCA, key Secretaries, CEA. Secretariat = FinMin's Dept of Economic Affairs. Body (sound-alikes) Detail FSB (2009, Basel) Financial Stability Board - G20 brainchild; global financial monitoring & regulator coordination. India has 3 seats (DEA Secretary, RBI Dy. Gov, SEBI chair). FATF (1989, Paris) Financial Action Task Force - G7 brainchild; anti-money-laundering & terror-finance; India joined 2010. IOSCO International body of securities regulators; SEBI is a member; famous for investor-protection guidelines. FSAP (WB + IMF) Financial Sector Assessment Program - 5-yearly survey; 1st for India 2011-12. NISM (SEBI, 2006) National Institute of Securities Markets - trains financial-market professionals (Budget-2023). 4. Company Types By incorporation:  Chartered (royal charter, e.g. East India Co 1600); Statutory (special Act - RBI, LIC, SBI); Registered (Companies Act - Tata, Infosys). Q - Private Ltd vs Public Ltd (Companies Act 2013)? Private Limited Public Limited Members: 2 to 200 Members: 7 to unlimited Cannot invite the public to buy shares/bonds Can invite public; if listed on an exchange = 'Listed' (e.g. Reliance), else 'Unlisted' (e.g. IPPB) Directors 2-15; governance norms relaxed Directors 3-15 (>=1 woman, >=1 resident Indian, 1/3rd independent); stricter governance IPO = 1st public share issue (private ltd converts to public ltd); FPO = a later issue.  Independent directors  protect minority shareholders. By ownership:  Govt/Public sector (Govt owns >=51%, e.g. SAIL, IPPB) vs Private (e.g. Reliance).  Holding company  owns majority in a  subsidiary  (Tata Sons -> TCS/Tata Steel). Misc:  One Person Company (OPC, single member); Not-for-Profit (GSTN, NPCI - profit reinvested, tax benefits); Dormant company; LLP (LLP Act 2008 - partners shielded from each other's misconduct); Partnership firm (Indian Partnership Act 1932 - joint liability). Small Companies (Budget-2021):  paid-up capital <= Rs.2 cr AND turnover <= Rs.20 cr -> compliance relief. 5. Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) Bodies Competition Commission of India (CCI):  prevents cartels/monopoly, protects consumers. MRTP Act 1970 -> Competition Act 2002 (CCI = 1 chairman + 6 members); appeals to NCLAT. MCA body (Companies Act 2013) Role NCLT / NCLAT Company-law cases, mergers, insolvency (IBC); appeal NCLAT -> SC. NFRA Sets & polices auditor/CA standards for listed & large firms; can debar; civil-court powers. IEPF Investor Education & Protection Fund - uses unclaimed shares/dividends for investor awareness (Budget-2023: reclaim portal). SFIO Serious Fraud Investigation Office - white-collar fraud; can search/seize/arrest; once it takes a case, others (CBI) can't proceed. IBBI Insolvency & Bankruptcy Board (also under MCA). Also under MCA:  ICAI (Chartered Accountants Act 1949), ICSI (Company Secretaries Act 1980), Institute of Cost Accountants (1959) - all have IPA status under IBC; Societies Registration Act 1860; e-gov portals SPICe+/MCA21 v3.0; officers via Indian Corporate Law Service (ICLS). 6. Corporate Governance & CSR Corporate governance:  term limits & women/independent directors, whistleblower protection, e-voting, company secretary etc. (Companies Act + SEBI directives). Key panel: Uday Kotak Committee (2017). Q - CSR - Corporate Social Responsibility? Mandate (Companies Act 2013):  spend 2% of the last 3 years' average profit on CSR (education, environment, health, sanitation, disaster mgmt). Applies to:  both public & private ltd with large profit/turnover/net worth. MCA gives National CSR Awards. Rule:  spending that directly benefits the company/its employees is NOT CSR. NSE Prime (2022):  voluntary higher corporate-governance standard for NSE-listed companies. BRSR:  Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report by SEBI (2012 BRR -> 2021 BRSR); top-listed firms disclose non-financial data (employee well-being, environment, human rights). 7. Takeover Terms Friendly takeover Hostile takeover Target's board approves the sale (e.g. Ranbaxy -> Sun Pharma) Buyer takes control without board consent (e.g. Elon Musk -> Twitter/X) Leveraged Buy-Out (LBO):  borrowing money to acquire majority stake (Musk buying Twitter). Poison Pill:  target issues extra shares to existing holders to make the buyer's stake unfavourable (anti-takeover defence). De-merger:  splitting one company into multiple companies. Key Facts (Quick Revision) Fact Detail SEBI Statutory 1992 (SCRA 1956); appeal SAT -> SC; chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey (2025). Securities Markets Code Bill 2025 Merges 3 laws; SEBI board -> 15; SEBI-Ombudsman. FSDC (2010) Chair = Finance Minister; regulator coordination. FSB / FATF FSB = G20 (Basel); FATF = G7 (Paris, anti-laundering). CCI Competition Act 2002 (from MRTP 1970); appeal NCLAT. CSR 2% of 3-yr avg profit (Companies Act 2013). BRSR SEBI; non-financial ESG disclosures by top-listed firms. Private vs Public Ltd 2-200 members vs 7-unlimited; only public can invite public.
